outcome: End-to-end tests that exercise scheduling, journal semantics, exactly-once and crash recovery run inside a worker sandbox through a test-only uncontained dispatch mode, while tests that prove isolation keep real containment - and no production binary can reach the uncontained path at all.

exclude: any runtime, manifest, config or environment route to uncontained dispatch in a production binary
changing what the isolation conformance cases assert

acceptance.text: A test-only uncontained dispatch mode exists and is reachable exclusively through an ldflags-linked gate, mirroring the existing test-hook gate: a binary built without that gate has no code path to uncontained dispatch, by manifest, config, environment or argument.

End-to-end tests whose subject is scheduling, journal semantics, exactly-once or crash recovery execute against the fake driver through the uncontained path and pass inside a worker sandbox where nested containment is impossible.

Tests whose subject is isolation - role, workspace, credential and process boundaries - continue to require real containment and are excluded from the uncontained path; their assertions are unchanged.
A test proves the negative: a production-configured binary refuses uncontained dispatch and reports it, so the gate cannot regress into a bypass unnoticed.

constraints: The gate follows the established test-hook pattern: linked through ldflags, absent from production builds, never reachable from runtime configuration.
What a worker proves by running the uncontained subset is orchestration correctness, not isolation; evidence must not claim otherwise.
Worker containment flags are unchanged; this slice adds no capability to any production binary.
The e2e check in this slice's own list is declared, not executed by a role (ADR 0010).
Check evidence belongs in the submission's checks field, never in files added to the repository; the candidate diff carries only product changes.
